audit.why: Cassiopeia takes levels 2-5 against a melee stacker with no poke, level 6 is a genuine skill check on Wither versus Petrifying Gaze, and Nasus flips it from first item. Both layers agree and the already-audited Nasus side reached the identical chart [Skill, Cassiopeia x3, Skill, Nasus, Nasus].

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither is the named matchup-defining cooldown in four fields with no duration or range, and Fury of the Sands was described only as giving 'lifesteal and size'.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s at 700 range - a 15-second window is long enough that baiting it is a real plan, and 700 range tells you how far outside it to stand. Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80s and deals percent-maximum-health damage while granting him bonus armour and magic resistance; 'lifesteal and size' is not what it does.
audit.corrected: 15s and 700 range added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, spikes[1].text and whys[5]; spikes[3].text now describes Fury of the Sands correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields tell the player to 'ground' Nasus with Miasma - spikes[2].text, early, wants.you[1], the tldr and dontsFull[1].d. Nasus has no dash, blink or movement ability, so the grounding half of Miasma is a non-interaction against him. Twin Fang was also written as 'Twin Fangs'.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Siphoning Strike is an attack modifier, Wither is a targeted slow, Spirit Fire is a ground-placed zone and Fury of the Sands is a self-buff. Nothing there is a movement ability. What Miasma actually does to Nasus is slow him out of caster-minion range and deny stacks - that is worth saying, and it is what the already-audited Nasus side concluded independently. Separately, Siphoning Strike carries an autoReset flag, so his damage arrives on an attack wind-up rather than on a visible cast.
audit.corrected: Every grounding claim replaced with the slow; the Siphoning Strike auto-reset tell added to report[5].t; name fixed to Twin Fang.

audit.why: The level-6 instruction to turn and face him for the full Petrifying Gaze stun is correct and is stated in spikes[1].text, mid, whys[4] and wants.you[2]. Riot's text: stuns enemies in front of her that are facing her, slows those with their back turned. The Nasus-side audit states the mirror of the same rule, so the two directions agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing about building into a Nasus who is about to gain bonus armour and magic resistance.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands grants him resistances on top of percent-max-health damage, so raw health on Cassiopeia is the wrong purchase against his ultimate window. Recorded rather than written because the only writable itemisation string here is a report entry I did not have a defensible band-safe rewrite for.
audit.corrected: Stated the percent-health consequence in spikes[3].text instead.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze answers his Wither all-in — when he slows you and walks in, turn and face him for the full stun, then chain Twin Fangs into the locked-down Nasus before the Wither runs its duration.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze answers his Wither all-in — when the 15s slow lands and he walks in, turn and face him for the full stun, then chain Twin Fang into the locked-down Nasus before Wither expires.

edits.before: Malignance or early Liandry's plus your leveling move speed make you a lane bully — perma-poke him off the wave, drop Miasma to ground and slow him out of caster-minion range, and slow his stacking.
edits.after: Malignance or early Liandry's plus your leveling move speed make you a lane bully — perma-poke him off the wave and use Miasma's slow to hold him out of caster-minion range; he has no dash for it to ground.

edits.before: Once Nasus is 2+ items his stacked Q one-shots, his E shreds your already-zero resistances, and R lifesteal lets him walk through your poison and Wither you to death — the lane has flipped to him, so the game must already be decided.
edits.after: Once Nasus is 2+ items his stacked Q one-shots, Spirit Fire shreds your already-zero resistances, and Fury of the Sands adds percent-max-health damage plus bonus armour and MR — buying health does not save you, so the game must already be decided.

edits.before: Nasus has no dash and no poke — he has to walk into auto range to last-hit with his empowered Q, and that is exactly where Cassiopeia lives. Open with Noxious Blast on the minion he is about to stack so you tag him for the move-speed proc and prime him, then Twin-Fang the poisoned Nasus for the heavily amplified hit while all he can answer with is a slow melee Q. At level 1 you have one ability and no real poison engine, so don't overcommit; from 2-3 your Q-into-E chain out-trades anything he does back, and Miasma's ground keeps him from simply walking onto the wave.
